record.original_question: What is the physical origin of Yukawa couplings in a fundamental theory that aims to extend the standard models of particle physics and cosmology?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the Standard Model of particle physics, the masses of the quarks and charged leptons, together with the CKM mixing matrix (and, in extensions, the PMNS matrix for neutrinos), are encoded in dimensionless Yukawa coupling matrices Y_u, Y_d, Y_e (and Y_ν) that appear in the gauge-invariant Lagrangian terms
  L_Yuk = − (Y_u)_{ij}  ar Q_{L,i} 	ilde H u_{R,j} − (Y_d)_{ij}  ar Q_{L,i} H d_{R,j} − (Y_e)_{ij}  ar L_{L,i} H e_{R,j} + h.c.,
where H is the Higgs doublet, 	ilde H = iσ_2 H^*, Q_L and L_L are the left-handed quark and lepton doublets, and u_R, d_R, e_R are the right-handed singlets, with i,j ∈ {1,2,3} flavor indices. Within the Standard Model these Yukawa matrices are free parameters: their numerical values (which span roughly twelve orders of magnitude from the electron Yukawa ~10^{-6} to the top Yukawa ~1) and their mixing structure are fitted to experiment rather than derived.

Problem: Construct a fundamental theory, extending the Standard Models of particle physics and cosmology, in which the Yukawa coupling matrices Y_u, Y_d, Y_e (and Y_ν) are not free parameters but are determined from first principles. Specifically, identify the physical/mathematical origin of these couplings — for instance from symmetry principles, geometric or topological data of an underlying space, dynamical (e.g., fixed-point) considerations, or other structural inputs — and show that the resulting predictions reproduce the observed fermion masses and mixing angles.
artifact.status_search_result: The origin of Yukawa couplings (the "flavor puzzle") is a long-standing open problem in fundamental physics. Many proposals exist — Froggatt–Nielsen mechanisms, extra-dimensional/string-theoretic constructions, modular flavor symmetries, GUT relations, anarchy hypotheses, etc. — but no derivation has been broadly accepted as explaining the observed pattern of fermion masses and mixings from first principles.

status_evidence.title: Flavour physics and CP violation (review)
status_evidence.snippet: The origin of the hierarchical pattern of fermion masses and mixings — the flavour puzzle — remains one of the most important open questions in particle physics.
status_evidence.claim: Origin of Yukawa/flavor structure is widely regarded as unsolved.

status_evidence.title: Modular flavor symmetry (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent approaches based on modular symmetries attempt to explain the Yukawa coupling structure, indicating the problem is still actively pursued.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on deriving Yukawa couplings, indicating the problem is open.
